title: "Signaling: Cond and Broadcast"

# Signaling: Cond and Broadcast

## Overview

Sometimes many waiters must wake when state changes. **Channels** cover most Go code; `sync.Cond` is the low-level “wait for condition under mutex” tool. Prefer channels unless you need broadcast to many waiters with shared state.

## Diagram: wait / signal

```text
sequence (top → bottom):
  actors: waiter, Cond, producer
  waiter --> Cond  : L.Lock
  waiter --> Cond  : Wait unlock+park
  producer --> Cond  : L.Lock change state
  producer --> Cond  : Signal or Broadcast
  producer --> Cond  : Unlock
  Cond --> waiter  : wake re-Lock
  waiter --> waiter  : recheck condition
```

## Pattern

```go
mu.Lock()
for !ready {
	cond.Wait() // unlocks mu while waiting
}
// ready == true
mu.Unlock()
```

**Always wait in a loop**—spurious or broad wakes happen.

## Signal vs Broadcast

| | Wake |
|--|------|
| `Signal` | one waiter |
| `Broadcast` | all waiters |

Wrong choice: Signal when many must proceed; Broadcast when one consumer would suffice (thundering herd).

## vs channel

| Need | Prefer |
|------|--------|
| One result / pipeline | channel |
| Close = fan-out “done” | close(ch) |
| Complex shared state predicate | Cond or simpler redesign |
| Select on many events | channels |

## Experiment

```go
var mu sync.Mutex
cond := sync.NewCond(&mu)
ready := false
go func() {
	time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
	mu.Lock()
	ready = true
	cond.Broadcast()
	mu.Unlock()
}()
mu.Lock()
for !ready {
	cond.Wait()
}
mu.Unlock()
```

**What to notice:** Waiter blocks without busy-spin; broadcast unblocks.

**Try next:** Rewrite with `close(done)` and compare readability.
